findings.issue: The footnote for the device paper is broken on 16 slides. Every \sref{Januar2026} without a page postnote prints 'Januar et al., Small Struct. 7, e202500807 (1 (2026)'. The new first-page rule compares the raw field with the literal 'e202500807 (1--12)', but the bibtex backend writes it as 'e202500807 (1\bibrangedash 12)' (build/main.bbl:1591). The comparison therefore fails and \mkfirstpage cuts at the dash. This is the most-cited reference in the talk, and the slides will be shown to its own authors.
findings.fix: Orchestrator only, since section authors may not edit the theme. In ntutalk.sty line 124, replace the literal test with \ifentrykeyequal{Januar2026}{e202500807}{...}, or compare against 'e202500807 (1\bibrangedash 12)'. Check the '850451 (1--7)' entry the same way. Rebuild and grep the PDF text for '(1 (2026)'.

summary:
The full build ran (bash tools/build.sh, about 43 s) and produced build/main.pdf with 117 pages. The footer counts 100 numbered frames: 81 talk frames from the outline to the next-steps slide, the Acknowledgements, 10 reference pages and 8 backup slides. The title, 14 part dividers, 'Thank you' and the backup divider are unnumbered. The build checks are clean: 0 errors, 0 undefined citations, 0 frame overflows, 0 overfull hboxes above 5 pt, 0 missing characters. Five small overfull boxes (0.7-2.9 pt) remain on PDF pages 25, 33, 70, 87 and 90, and hyperref warns about the math in the title. I rendered all pages to build/deck_png at 55 dpi and opened every one; I also opened selected pages at 110 dpi in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-iwo-tft-tcad-dft/766c6a12-f4a6-5e51-9cad-484b1261a35f/scratchpad/hi. Page numbers in the findings are PDF pages.

Three problems should be fixed before presenting:
1. The device-paper footnote prints as 'Januar et al., Small Struct. 7, e202500807 (1 (2026)' on 16 slides. The theme's literal comparison does not match the bibtex '\bibrangedash' form. This needs an orchestrator fix in ntutalk.sty.
2. Internal bib notes are printed in the reference list, including 'read by Astra', 'METADATA_REQUIRES_VERIFICATION' and the 'installed copy' note on the ATLAS manual.
3. The Acknowledgements slide claims that all hypotheses and read-out rules were registered before the outcomes were known. The deck itself contradicts this (S0/S1 seen before the freeze, A1 written after its measured values, A38/A42/A43). The same slide also prints an empty Silvaco footnote, '[3] ()'.

Most numbers agree across sections:
- Thresholds 0.662/0.644/0.083 V and the misses −0.29/−0.37/−0.23 V.
- The SS windows, ΔEg 0.335/0.900 eV, ΔEc +0.281/+0.848 eV and ΔEv −0.054/−0.052 eV.
- Mass 0.1541 m0, the Kane check (1 % / 10 %) and the W level 1.22-1.80 eV.
- Donated densities 1.4-3.0e21 (bulk 2.7e21), the H-L numbers and the S1-05 result (+142 mV) with audit A13.
- The launch counts (14 seen, 17 of 200 used) and the dates (freeze 2026-10-10T18:33:13Z, A37, D-43).

The main inconsistencies are:
- ΔEc(2 nm) = 0.353 eV (the model V1 law) is shown on p30 without saying so, against 0.28 eV in Part 6.
- 'The step' means 0.56 V in Parts 1-2 and 0.579 V in Parts 10 and 14.
- Labels clash: V1/V2 are both model versions and corrections; C2-C4, C1-C6, C10 and C0xx overlap; S1 is both a window and a stage; T2/T3 are undefined.
- The H-E status differs between p21 and p115, and the spin-moment range differs between p63 and p116.
- Notation drifts (Nc/NC, NV/Nv/N_VB, W_TA/W_T), and p114 uses a non-standard 'calculated' label.

On flow, the story runs coherently from motivation to conclusions, but the talk is about twice too long and needs cutting to roughly 35-45 frames. Part 4 uses the DFT laws before Parts 5-7 introduce them. Part 3 front-loads four dense register tables. S0-S2, V0, T2/T3 and the amendment numbers are used before they are defined. The 'strongly supported' swing-collapse result in the conclusions has no slide anywhere in the deck. Several slides duplicate each other: p86 is nearly identical to backup p111 and still says 'backup slide'; p38 and p91; p39 and p62; p93/p94 and p95.

Visually, about 45 slides use centred frames while the rest use [t]. The conclusion and register slides are walls of scriptsize text. Ledger IDs, commit hashes and file names inside bullets look machine-made. Citation marks in \src lines are set too large, the reference list keeps the default beamer icons and spills onto a 10th page with one entry, and several result slides have no take-away.

No blind-analysis violations were found. There are no amorphous electronic values and no ATLAS results from S2 on. The only risk is the p80 wording about a 'W + 6 O state localised at 0.7, 0.8 and 2.0 nm', which should be reworded as hypothetical. There are no superseded statements: V12 is stated correctly on p40, p112 and p116, H-L is unresolved, the 6.3 nm predictions are falsified, µsat is inferred as the leading candidate, the 2.7e21 donated density and −0.052 eV valence shift are correct, and W is described as a resonant donor everywhere except where old wording is quoted as a correction.
